newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ENI sees sharp rise in upstream investment.
newsitem.headline: ENI sees sharp rise in upstream investment.

text.p: Italian oil company ENI SpA expects to boost annual investment in upstream operations --- exploration and energy production -- to some five trillion lire in 2000 from 2.5-3.0 trillion in 1996, managing director Franco Bernabe said.
He said total ENI investment in the 1997-2000 four-year period would be 35,000 trillion lire, of which an average 52 percent would be in AGIP, its upstream company.
Bernabe said that the overall level of group investment in the four-year period would not show any significant increase from earlier levels.
The big change was in the mix, he said.
"There is going to be a strong shift towards exploration and production," he told journalists at the World Economic Forum, a meeting of government and business leaders in this Swiss mountain resort.

Ninety percent of ENI's total investment over the four-year period will be in energy with the aim of lifting output of oil and gas to 1.2 million barrels per day equivalent against some 900,000-one million at present.
The main area of new development will be in central Asia, the areas of the former Soviet Union.
